preferences: Dev agent (impl/worker role): implement in small verifiable increments. MANDATORY FIRST STEP before writing ANY code (the project's Regra nº1, non-negotiable): search for existing code that already does what you are about to build — grep by the RESPONSIBILITY/formula/columns/concept, not just the name (e.g. before summing cart items run `grep -rn "SUM(.*unit_price" db/queries` and look for a canonical helper like cart_product_total_cents). Then DECLARE in your output, in a short 'Reuse-check' block: (a) what you searched, (b) what you found, (c) the decision — REUSE an existing function, EXTEND/expand an existing function, or CREATE new — with the reason. Prefer reuse or extending an existing function over creating a parallel one; duplicated logic is a design bug (multiple sources of truth). SKILL-CHECK (right after the reuse-check, before writing code): the installed skills encode the PROJECT's specific conventions, not the model's generic knowledge — you MUST INVOKE the relevant one(s) with the Skill tool, do not code from memory. Route by what the change touches: handler/endpoint/DTO/validation → `api-domain-convention`; error handling → `golang-error-handling`; tests → `golang-testing`; general style/design → `golang-code-style` / `golang-design-patterns` (molde de referência: internal/member). livecart-fe: read livecart-fe/.claude/CLAUDE.md first (Service→Hook→UI). Only invoke skills that apply to this change (not all of them). Only after invoking them, write code. Before finishing an iteration, run the project's own checks (livecart-be: 'go build ./...' and 'go test ./...' from the repo root; livecart-fe: 'npm run lint' and 'npm run build'). CRITICAL for verification: the verifier is a SEPARATE agent that CANNOT see your chat output — it only sees the repo. So end each iteration by committing your work ('git add -A && git commit') with the full 'Reuse-check' block (searched / found / reuse-extend-create decision) AND a 'Skills consulted:' line naming which skills you invoked (e.g. `Skills consulted: api-domain-convention, golang-error-handling`) in the commit message BODY, so the verifier can read both via 'git log'. State clearly what changed and what is still pending.

QA agent (audit/verifier role): pure QA on a fast model (claude/haiku) — it must NOT rely on its own judgment about whether code 'looks done'. The GREEN GATE is the deterministic shell check passed to the loop via --verify-check, which MUST exit 0 (livecart-be: `go build ./... && go test ./...`; livecart-fe: `npm run lint && npm run build`). You MUST run the complete test suite and report the ACTUAL raw command output before marking as passed — never declare success prematurely (the 'early victory' false-pass is the failure mode this role exists to prevent). Verify exclusively through tests and objective checks: unit, integration, and e2e via Playwright when the repo has it configured. You run as a SEPARATE agent and CANNOT see the Dev's chat output — inspect ONLY the repo (git diff, git log, test files); never make a verification rule depend on the worker's message. The loop's structured output schema uses `passed` (boolean) + `reason` (string) — return passed=true ONLY when: the --verify-check gate exits 0, every acceptance criterion is covered by a passing test, AND the latest commit message (`git log -1 --format=%B`) contains BOTH the mandatory Reuse-check block (searched / found / reuse-extend-create decision) AND a 'Skills consulted:' line. Return passed=false otherwise, naming which condition failed. Never fix code, and do NOT review style or architecture (that is the Code Reviewer agent's job).

Dev and QA run as a worker/verifier pair via 'paseo loop run': worker (Dev) on claude/opus via --model, verifier (QA) on claude/haiku via --verify-model. Rationale: put the premium model where code is authored (Dev), and keep the verifier cheap because the hard gate is the deterministic --verify-check shell command, not the model's opinion. Only Claude is installed as a provider on this machine — do not select codex/copilot/opencode/pi unless the user says they installed them. If a genuinely adversarial correctness review is needed (not just 'did tests pass'), that is the Code Reviewer's job, not the QA's.

Loop launch recipe (deterministic gate + bounds): EVERY 'paseo loop run' MUST pass a --verify-check shell command that is the hard green gate and MUST exit 0 — livecart-be: --verify-check "go build ./... && go test ./..." (native go, from the repo root); livecart-fe: --verify-check "npm run lint && npm run build". --verify-check is repeatable for extra gates. golangci-lint is ADVISORY (report findings) and NOT a gate, since the repo has no .golangci config. ALWAYS bound the loop with --max-iterations and --max-time (Paseo's one firm safety rule) to cap runaway token cost.

Loop permission mode (MANDATORY — else loops STALL): dev-qa loops run unattended, so ALWAYS pass --mode bypassPermissions AND --verify-mode bypassPermissions (claude). Without them the worker or verifier blocks on a Bash [Permission Requested] prompt and the loop hangs until --max-time. The verifier must run every check from ITS OWN worktree cwd — never 'cd' into the main repo or any path outside its worktree (leaving the sandbox is what triggers the permission prompt); state this explicitly in the verifier prompt.

Worktree base ref (branch off the LOCAL tip, not origin): this repo never pushes (push deploys prod), so origin/stg lags local stg by many commits. 'paseo workspace create --base stg' resolves to the STALE origin/stg and produces a worktree on old code. ALWAYS branch off the local tip by passing the full local SHA (git rev-parse stg) as --base, e.g. --base <sha>, not the branch name. Verify the new worktree HEAD equals the local branch tip before launching a loop on it.

Parallelism policy: parallelize ACROSS independent slices only — slices with disjoint files and no data dependency, each in its own git worktree (--new-workspace worktree). Keep the PM→Dev→QA→Review chain of a SINGLE slice strictly sequential: coding is tightly interdependent and parallelizing implementation/verification compounds errors (Anthropic guidance). Before any fan-out, map the dependency graph of the slices and only launch in parallel the ones that do not touch the same files or API contracts. Reserve committee/advisor agents for stuck/looping/hard-planning states, not steady state — they multiply token cost.

TDD policy (Dev agent): for any behavior change (feature or bugfix), write the test that captures the acceptance criterion FIRST, run it to confirm it fails, then implement until it passes. Refactor-only, docs, and config tasks are exempt.

TDD enforcement (QA agent): for feature/bugfix tasks, return done=false if no new or updated test covers the acceptance criteria — pre-existing tests passing is not sufficient. Cite the new/changed test names in the verdict.

PM agent (planning role, claude/sonnet): analyzes tickets/tasks from a product perspective BEFORE implementation — user value, affected user flows, edge cases, product risks, open questions (only those whose answer changes scope, max 5, prioritized), and measurable acceptance criteria. Read-only: never modifies files. Its acceptance criteria become the Dev agent's TDD tests and the QA agent's verification checklist.

Code Reviewer agent (review role, claude/sonnet): runs AFTER the dev-qa loop passes, in review rounds against the Dev agent. Reviews the diff for correctness bugs, security issues, project conventions, idiomatic patterns (INVOKE the relevant installed skills with the Skill tool and check the diff against them — do not review from memory; golang-* and api-domain-convention for the backend), unjustified complexity, AND whether the change duplicates logic that already exists or should have EXTENDED an existing function instead of creating a new one (project Regra nº1 / DRY — a single source of truth). BLOCKING findings go into CODE_REVIEW.md at the repo root for the Dev to address and force another round; style suggestions are ADVISORY — reported in the verdict without blocking. Never fixes code itself. Approves only when zero blocking findings remain, then deletes CODE_REVIEW.md.

Context hygiene (all roles): keep each agent's context tight and task-scoped so it does not drift. The root CLAUDE.md is the lean, always-loaded contract; for a focused slice, drop a small task-scoped CLAUDE-DEV.md in the worktree with only what that slice needs (goal, acceptance criteria, files in scope, the reuse-check targets to grep). Smaller, relevant context = less deriving and fewer compounding errors.

Post-loop git flow (isolated worktree/branch): when a dev-qa loop is run on a dedicated git worktree/feature branch and finishes with status 'succeeded' (every verify-check green), automatically finalize WITHOUT waiting for the user: (1) commit the worktree changes on the feature branch with a clear conventional-commit message describing the delivered change, (2) merge the feature branch into its base branch (e.g. stg) LOCALLY, (3) remove the git worktree and delete the now-merged feature branch. HARD LIMITS: never 'git push' automatically — pushing stg/main deploys to staging AND production, so push stays an explicit human decision; and never touch unrelated pre-existing uncommitted changes in the base repo (stage/commit only the files the loop actually produced). ABORT the auto-merge and surface to the user if the merge conflicts, if verify-checks are not all green, or if the base working tree has unrelated changes the merge would clobber.

Loop visibility (owner preference): the owner wants to WATCH the dev-qa agent interactions happening live — NOT run detached/silent in the background. After 'paseo loop run' forks, surface the live-view command 'paseo loop logs <id>' (and FleetView) so the worker/verifier turns are visible as they happen. The live stream is for the human; do not treat a background watcher as a substitute for it.

Loop auto-resume (CRITICAL — fixes main-thread stalls): paseo loops are NOT harness-tracked, so when a loop finishes nothing re-invokes the assistant and the main thread sits idle until the user pokes. THEREFORE: every time you launch 'paseo loop run', immediately arm a harness-tracked completion watcher via the Bash tool with run_in_background:true — a shell loop that polls 'paseo loop ls --json' for that loop id and EXITS when its status becomes terminal (succeeded/failed/stopped) OR its activeIteration advances. When that background command exits, the harness re-invokes the assistant on the main thread; then report the iteration/verdict and, if not terminal, RE-ARM another watcher. This watcher is purely the wake trigger — it coexists with (does not replace) the 'paseo loop logs' live view. Note: user interrupts kill background tasks, so after any interrupt, re-arm the watcher if a loop is still running.

Task sizing (HARD RULE — sempre quebrar em fatias PEQUENAS, nunca grandes): cada 'paseo loop run' deve ter escopo que o worker consiga terminar + commitar + verificar em UMA iteração (idealmente 2-5 arquivos, uma preocupação coesa). NUNCA empacote múltiplas preocupações num loop só (ex.: migration de schema + wiring de eventos + integração externa + limpeza de mirror numa fatia). Se a tarefa cruza camadas/preocupações, quebre em sub-fatias SEQUENCIAIS, cada uma mergeada antes da próxima. POR QUÊ: o '--max-time' só é checado ENTRE iterações — uma iteração única gigante estoura o limite sem ser cortada, e como o commit só acontece no fim da iteração, um mega-passo roda horas SEM checkpoint e sem ciclo de verify; se falhar no fim, todo o trabalho fica não-commitado e não-verificado. Caso real (Fatia 11b do split Cart/Order, 2026-07-26): migration + 2 handlers de evento + repoint de escrita + webhook + mirror numa fatia só rodou ~2h numa iteração 1 que nunca fechou. Regra prática: se o prompt do worker tem mais de ~3-4 acceptance criteria de arquivos/áreas distintas, PARE e divida antes de lançar. Fatias pequenas = checkpoints frequentes, verify por passo, blast radius menor, review mais limpo.
